method: A rule is composed from six optional decisions in a fixed order: SUBSYSTEM, KERNEL, up to two attribute matches, SYMLINK, OWNER, GROUP and MODE. The subsystem is required and is lowercase letters, digits, underscores or hyphens, written as udev reports it (tty, usb, block, net). The kernel name pattern accepts the usual glob syntax, * ? and character classes such as ttyUSB[0-9] or ttyUSB*|ttyACM*, and is left out when the field is blank. Each attribute match needs both a sysfs attribute name (letters, digits and underscores) and a value; the target selector chooses ATTR, which reads the attribute on the device the event is for, or ATTRS, which searches that device and its parents, where a USB serial adapter's idVendor and idProduct are found. Values are quoted in the rule and may contain spaces, but a double quote or backslash is refused because udev would require it escaped. A link name must be one path component of at most 63 characters from letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, with no slash, space or % substitution; SYMLINK adds the name beside the kernel-assigned one. Owner and group accept a name or a numeric id up to 4294967294; MODE accepts three or four octal digits and is normalised to four, at most 0777, so setuid, setgid and sticky bits are not offered. The result reports the exact rule line, its length and clause count, the rule file name derived from the link or subsystem (a 99- prefix so it runs after the distribution's own rules) and the reload and trigger commands. Warnings appear when a rule only matches without assigning anything, when nothing narrows it to a device, when MODE is set without OWNER or GROUP, and when permissions change without a SYMLINK. The page composes text only: it reads no device data, installs nothing and uses no network.

sources.title: udev(7), systemd manual: rule files are read in lexical order from /etc/udev/rules.d, and matching keys SUBSYSTEM, KERNEL, ATTR, ATTRS and SYMLINK build one rule per line.
systemd-udevd.service(8): rules are applied when a device is added, and udevadm control --reload-rules plus udevadm trigger apply an edited rule to existing devices.
udevadm(8): control --reload-rules reloads rule files and trigger --subsystem-match replays events for one subsystem.
